ph-mounted.title: Mounted rules: Charge (Yah!), Serpentine, Spurs
ph-mounted.source: Pistolheart Volume 1, printed page 7 (PDF page 10), "Optional Rules for Mounted PCs"
ph-mounted.text:
- Mounts don't have their own stats and can't be targeted by adversaries. Exceptions to this are PCs mounted on creatures with their own stat blocks, such as a ranger's animal companion, or a druid in Beastform.
- Mounts can suffer consequences as a result of a PC rolling with Fear.
- A mounted rider automatically succeeds on rolls to outrun or catch up to someone on foot.
- Once per long rest, a mounted rider can take a short rest while on the move.
- If a PC's mount isn't present in a scene, but the mount could reasonably reach the PC, they can give the GM a Fear to whistle for any number of mounts, involving them in the scene.
- While mounted, PCs can move within Far range and can use the following abilities:
  - Charge: Make a Strength roll. On a success, you move in a line to Far range, passing through any adversaries in your path.
  - Serpentine: When you are targeted by an attack, while mounted, you can mark a Stress to make an Instinct reaction roll. On a success, you gain a bonus to your Evasion against the attack equal to your tier.
  - Spurs: Make an Agility Roll to move within Very Far range.

ph-saddles.title: Magic Saddles
ph-saddles.source: Pistolheart Volume 3, printed page 34 (PDF page 34), "Magic Saddles"
ph-saddles.text: These saddles adjust to fit the size of the mount. A PC and their mount can only benefit from the effects of a single saddle at a time.

ph-infusions.title: Infusions
ph-infusions.text: Infusions are a new type of feature that you can add to an item, wearable object, or layer onto a weapon or armor. Operating similarly to the "Touched" domain cards, a PC must have a majority of their domain cards of the corresponding type in their loadout to benefit from the infused feature. If an Infusion is placed on a weapon or armor, it exists alongside the original feature and does not replace it. A PC can hold 1 Infused item at a time. At tier 3, they can hold 2 Infused items, but can only benefit from one Infusion at a time.

ph-most-wanted.title: Most Wanted (Corrupt Sheriff)
ph-most-wanted.source: Pistolheart Volume 2, Corrupt Sheriff (Tier 2 Leader) stat block, "Most Wanted - Action"
ph-most-wanted.text: Most Wanted - Action: Spend 2 Fear to make a PC Most Wanted. A Most Wanted PC has disadvantage on Presence Rolls in civilized locations. A Most Wanted PC can clear the condition by spending a chest of gold to pay the bounty or by finding another way to clear their name.

While wearing this bandolier, you can spend a Hope during a moment of calm to change the damage type of one of your firearms from physical to magic or from magic to physical until your next rest.
While wearing this bandit mask, you don't count as Most Wanted, but have disadvantage on Presence Rolls.

This gleaming, wide-brimmed cowboy hat never seems to get dirty or damaged. When it catches the sun just right, the light of justice seems to radiate off you. While wearing this hat, you have advantage on Presence Rolls when dealing with the Law.

You save time quickly unpacking your gear when you use a downtime move on a short rest. When you roll a die to determine how many Armor Slots, Stress, or Hit Points you clear, you can use the die's maximum result instead.
When you fail an attack roll made with a firearm, you can spend a Hope to make the target mark a Hit Point, and describe the elaborate path your bullet takes to hit the target.

You can drink this dubious looking liquid to roll a d6. On a result of 2 or higher, you gain a +2 bonus on action and damage rolls until the end of the scene. On a result of 1, you gain a -1 penalty to action and damage rolls until the end of the scene.
You can imbibe a dram of this tincture to clear up to 12 Stress, then mark a Stress that can't be cleared by any means until you take a long rest.
***Turn Tail:*** As a reaction, when you take Severe damage you can move up to Close range.
***Sand Strider:*** -1 to Agility. You can move up to Close range through dirt or sand, underground, as part of an action.
***Macabre:*** An undead adversary must mark a Stress the first time it attacks you in a scene.
***Death's Acolyte:*** Once per scene, when you fail an attack roll you can mark a Stress to force the target to mark a Hit Point.
Mark a Hit Point and a Stress to drink this spirit. On your next successful attack, you automatically deal maximum damage.
Shred this origami horse to immediately become mounted on a paper horse. The paper horse lasts until the end of the scene, until you dismount it, or until you take Severe damage while mounted.
If the PC holding this paw fails a roll, they can give the GM 3 Fear to turn that failure into a critical success, and become Vulnerable until the end of the scene.
Spend a Hope to make your mount sprout wings, allowing it to fly until the end of the scene. While the wings are out, you can spend 3 Hope to allow any allied mounts within Far range to fly with you.
When you Yah! (PHv1, pg7), you can mark a Stress to deal d4+4 physical damage using your tier to targets you pass through whose Difficulty you meet.
As an action, you can make your mount disappear into the saddle until you spend a Hope to summon it.
While mounted, you can spend a handful of gold in place of marking an Armor Slot.

Once per scene, while mounted, you can extend an air bubble around you to Very Close range. The air bubble moves with you and lasts until the end of the scene, or you dismount. Creatures and solid objects can pass freely through the bubble, but gases and liquids are kept out.
You gain a bonus equal to your tier on Strength and Agility rolls to perform tricks and acrobatic feats while mounted.
Once per scene, on a successful attack that deals magic damage, increase your proficiency by 1. The first time in a scene you deal Severe magic damage, gain a Hope.
Once per scene, on a successful attack that deals physical damage, increase your proficiency by 1. The first time in a scene you deal Severe physical damage, gain a Hope.
At the beginning of a scene, you gain a +1 bonus to Evasion until you take damage. The first time in a scene that you avoid damage, gain a Hope.

Once per long rest, you can add an additional grimoire card of level 3 or lower from your vault into your loadout, which does not count against your maximum loadout size. You can use this grimoire card once before it returns to your vault.
Once per scene, when you make an Adversary mark a Stress, you can make them mark an additional Stress and gain a Hope.
Once per rest, if you roll a success with Hope on an attack and your Fear roll is 1 lower than your Hope roll, you roll a critical success instead.
Once per rest, gain a special Armor Slot that you can only mark if it's your last Armor Slot. When you mark this Armor Slot, clear a Hit Point and gain a Hope.
Once per session, when you make yourself or another PC clear any number of Hit Points, the target clears a Stress for each Hit Point cleared.
Once per scene, you can spend Hope instead of marking Armor Slots to reduce the damage severity.
